newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed strongly higher for the fourth straight session in very active trading on Monday, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.24 percent, or 2.82 points, to 225.01 on high all-share turnover of 156 million shekels against 147 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index climbed 1.21 percent to 232.75.

"The main reason for the rise of the last days is that the provident funds have started buying shares," said Amir Eayal of Epsilon Securities. "There is a general consensus that the market will continue to rise in 1997."
"Another (interest) rate cut will bring new money into the market and this will lead to another rise," he added.

"The positive trend in the market is continuing and we can see a real change. The increased activity and the improvement of the small capitalization stocks (traded on the Caram) are a clear sign of a bull market," said Eli Nahum head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"The market does not need any particular reason to rise. It is attractive and all the technical indicators show that the crisis has ended," Nahum added.

The most active shares was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 1.5 percent to 1,797 agorot on volume of 11 million shekels, following a sharp rise in Sunday. Bank Hapoalim, the number two volume leader, gained 1.0 percent to 542 agorot on turnover of 5.2 million shekels. Koor Industries lost 1.0 percent to 28,751 agorot on volume of 4.7 million shekels.
